purpose: Resume data preparation across Codex accounts, chats, agent sessions, connector link changes and machines without repeating accepted work.

authority.data_identity: Existing immutable payload file IDs plus SHA256 and byte counts in member_catalog.json.
authority.runtime_identity: Freshly verify the owner-selected Google profile outside task specs. Resolve the current connector link at runtime; never treat link ID, Codex account, chat or agent session as data authority.
authority.historical_identity: data_owner_history records past publication identities only; it does not assert present Drive ownership or grant access.
authority.permissions: Exact-ID metadata/read succeeds only proves read access. Require independently observed can_update=true or equivalent explicit update-right evidence before updates; never infer write permission from read permission.
authority.no_duplicate_recovery: If an expected ID is unreadable or rights are unproven, preserve the existing checkpoint and report access failure. Do not create a replacement folder, copy data, share files or change permissions.

checkpoint_contents: Hash-addressed portable task specs and finite queue, independent of runtime identities and artifact locators.
Persistent leased worker attempt, expiry, next unconsumed line and source/split/token audit evidence references.
Completed result keyed by task content hash; exact result digest; conflicting results require review.
Immutable data artifact IDs/hashes; mutable control pointers contain ID only and use fresh raw verification/revision.
pinned_input_state_sha256 is historical provenance, not a requirement that updated STATE retain its old hash. No self hash is embedded in mutable STATE.
handoff_steps: Read the same existing STATE/control ID and portable checkpoint, not a chat summary. Preserve all 31 immutable payload artifact references and the original control IDs.

Resolve current Google connector and verify chosen profile. Verify required immutable payload exact ID, full bytecount/SHA256 before consuming it. Freshly raw-read mutable controls and validate a monotonic checkpoint revision.

Load persistent ledger/export, inspect completed tasks before claiming work. Do not rerun accepted110 or completed task hashes. Reclaim only expired leases; old lease token cannot acknowledge after reclaim.

Index explicit valid source members before corresponding chat members. Carry the same SQLite database with the handoff; it stores committed row cursor, source raw/canonical hashes and field fingerprints, sample/mode uniqueness, global split keys, token measurements and issues.

Consume bounded chunks. Commit successful row effects and cursor in one SQLite transaction. After interruption reopen database and replay only the current gzip/member to the first unconsumed row. No payload extraction or whole-corpus download is required.

Use one coordinator to merge exported completed results idempotently; verify artifact identities, task and result hashes, then reject conflicts. Reload/check revision immediately before saving to existing control ID and raw-readback verify after save.

One-coordinator optimistic read-before-write is not atomic compare-and-swap across independent Drive writers. Cross-machine simultaneous writers must be serialized; separate SQLite files or Drive sync do not provide a distributed lock.
Keep frozen V3/V4, sealed challenge, pilot and superseded audit payloads separate. Compare permitted existing hash/signature metadata only. Never open sealed/pilot content for tuning.

Publish all required code, catalog, exported queue/results and database evidence into the existing publication/checkpoint flow only after root review. These files currently remain bounded local evidence; this agent made no Drive calls.
